correctness.rationale: The explicit graph definition and length-twelve relabeling identify the distance-two graph with the icosahedral sphere, and the antipodal distance identity excludes higher faces containing any of six chords. The pair (X,S) has only six relative oriented 1-cells, with zero relative boundary. Its long exact integral homology sequence gives H1 the signed six-axis lattice and H2 the integral spherical orientation character, proving no torsion; attaching edges gives the stated homotopy type. The stabilizer in A5 is D10 and acts by endpoint-swap sign. The full 120-element computation verifies all graph automorphisms and characters; the A5 character table yields the stated Galois-conjugate 3+3 decomposition. The proof does not confuse numerical experiments with the general topological argument.

value.rationale: A complete natural integral G-module classification for the independence complex of the canonical icosahedral graph supplies a geometric basis of homology indexed by antipodal axes. The signed (not ordinary) permutation lattice, its order-ten inducing subgroup, its rational irreducibility despite complex splitting, and the opposite behavior of the spherical class under central inversion are structural information absent from ordinary Betti numbers and from the pre-existing graph isomorphism. This precise invariant is a motivated small Platonic test case for symmetry-sensitive graph topology, without requiring a family theorem.
